# JavaScript Agent Guidelines

## Verification

Inspect the `scripts` field in `package.json` and run the relevant scripts, fixing all
reported errors and warnings. Only run scripts that exist. Do not infer style preferences
from training data — defer to the tools configured for this repo.

- **Formatting** — run the format script; if none exists, check for a formatter config
  (e.g. `.prettierrc.*`, `prettier.config.*`, `oxfmt.toml`) and invoke it directly; note
  the linter (e.g. ESLint, oxlint) may serve as the formatter via `--fix`
- **Linting** — run the lint script; if none exists, check for a linter config
  (e.g. `eslint.config.*`, `.eslintrc.*`, `oxlint.json`) and invoke it directly
- **Tests** — commonly named `test`, `unit`, or similar
- **Understanding rules** — read the linter and formatter config files in the repo root
  rather than guessing

## Dependencies

Verify any library you use exists in `package.json`. If a new dependency is needed, add
it via the package manager rather than editing `package.json` directly.

## Security

- Avoid `eval()` and `innerHTML` assignments from untrusted input

## Tests

Write tests for any new functionality. Check the test config for enforced coverage
thresholds; if none exist, aim for meaningful coverage of main code paths and edge cases.

## Code Practices

### Breaking Changes

- When changing a function or module interface, update all affected call sites in the
  same change.

### Modules & Imports

- Use ES modules (`import` / `export`)

### Functions

- Prefer early returns to reduce nesting over deeply nested `if/else` chains

### Immutability

- Avoid mutating function arguments or shared state; return new values instead

### Magic Values

- Avoid inline literal strings and numbers whose meaning is not obvious from
  context; assign them to named constants (e.g. status codes, limits, timeouts,
  fixed identifiers) — not for universally understood values like `0`, `1`, or
  loop indices

### Async Code

- Prefer `async`/`await` over nested promise chains
- Always handle rejected promises explicitly or propagate them to the caller

### Error Handling

- Throw `Error` instances or project-specific error types — not strings or plain objects

### Comments

- Use JSDoc for exported functions, classes, and constants where the name and
  signature alone do not convey intent, accepted value ranges, or side effects
- Add inline comments to explain _why_ a non-obvious decision was made, not to
  restate what the code does
- Do not add comments that describe obvious code or above every function by default

# JavaScript Library / Component Agent Guidelines

## Code Location

Locate the `package.json` file first; front-end code is located at `src` relative to
its location.

## Versioning

If the `version` field in `package.json` has not already been updated relative to the
main branch, ask the developer what version to set before making any changes (see
[semver](https://semver.org)). Set it once and do not change it again.

## README

Update `README.md` when a change affects the public API, usage, configuration, or
any documented behavior. Do not update it for internal refactors or fixes that have
no user-facing effect.

## CHANGELOG

Maintain a changelog using the [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com) format.
The file may be named `CHANGELOG.md` or `RELEASE-NOTES.md` — check the repo root for
an existing file before assuming the name. Add an entry under the `[Unreleased]` section
for every change, using the appropriate category:

- **Added** — new functionality
- **Changed** — changes to existing functionality
- **Deprecated** — functionality to be removed in a future release
- **Removed** — functionality removed in this release
- **Fixed** — bug fixes
- **Security** — security-related fixes

If no changelog file exists, create `CHANGELOG.md` with the following structure:

# TypeScript Agent Guidelines

## Verification

- **Type checking** — commonly named `typecheck`, `type-check`, or similar
- **Builds** — commonly named `build` or similar when declaration output or package
  exports are affected
- **TypeScript config** — read `tsconfig.json` and any extended configs before changing
  compiler options or module syntax

## Dependencies

- Do not add a separate `@types/*` package until checking whether the dependency already
  ships its own types
- Keep runtime dependencies and `devDependencies` separate; type-only tooling usually
  belongs in `devDependencies`

## Security

- Treat external data (`fetch`, JSON files, environment variables, storage, request
  bodies) as `unknown` until validated or narrowed

## Tests

For exported types, public package APIs, or declaration output, include compile-time
coverage through the existing type-check script, type tests, or tests that compile
consumer-shaped usage.

## Code Practices

### Modules & Imports

- Use `import type` and `export type` for type-only imports and exports
- Follow the repository's configured module format and file extensions (`.ts`, `.mts`,
  `.cts`); include runtime import extensions when the project requires them
- Avoid exporting incidental implementation types from dependencies unless they are
  intentionally part of the public API

### Types

- Treat `tsconfig.json` as the source of truth; do not loosen strictness to make an
  implementation compile unless explicitly requested
- Avoid `any`; use `unknown` for untrusted or unclear values and narrow before use
- Do not use type assertions as conversions or validation; only assert when the code has
  already proven the condition and TypeScript cannot infer it
- Define explicit input and output types at public module boundaries
- Prefer type inference for local variables when the inferred type is clear
- Model constrained states with unions or discriminated unions instead of broad strings,
  numbers, or booleans
- Avoid non-null assertions unless the code has already proved the condition that
  TypeScript cannot express
- Use exhaustive `never` checks when switching over discriminated unions or finite state
  variants
- Use `satisfies` for configuration objects when you need shape checking without
  widening literal types
- Distinguish optional and nullable fields intentionally; do not interchange `foo?: T`
  and `foo: T | null` unless the domain treats absence and null the same way
- Avoid broad or inaccurate index signatures; type only the fields you need or use
  `unknown` plus narrowing for unstructured data
- When `erasableSyntaxOnly`, `isolatedModules`, or similar settings are enabled, avoid
  TypeScript constructs that require runtime transforms such as `enum`, namespaces, and
  parameter properties

### Type Organization

- Define types close to the code that owns them by default
- Move shared types to an existing shared type module only after they are used by
  multiple modules
- Do not create a broad `types.ts` file or `types/` dumping ground unless the repo
  already uses that convention
- Keep public API types exported from the same entry point as the functions or
  components that consume them
- Keep private helper types unexported
- Verify declaration output still exposes the intended public types after moving or
  renaming type definitions

### Functions

- Include explicit return types for exported functions

### Error Handling

- Narrow caught errors before reading custom properties because catch values may be
  `unknown`

### Comments

- JSDoc on exported symbols improves generated `.d.ts` declaration output
